```{r setup, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, include = FALSE}
# echo = TRUE for all code-blocks:
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

# Cleaning:
rm(list = ls())
cat("\14")
graphics.off()

# Packages:
packages <- c("tidyverse", "cowplot", "readODS", "plotly", "lintr", "here")
for (i in packages) {
  if (!require(i, character.only = TRUE)) install.packages(i)
  library(i, character.only = TRUE)
  print(paste("Is package", i, "loaded?", i %in% loadedNamespaces()))
}

# Load data:
getwd()
file.exists("scripts/01-get-data.R")
source(here::here("scripts", "01-get-data.R"))
```


## **Part A: Replicate this plot**


### Prepare data

```{r data-prep-1, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
school_provider <- eindscores |>
  select(INSTELLINGSCODE, matches("_(AANTAL|GEM)$")) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = matches("_(AANTAL|GEM)$"),
    names_to = c("provider", ".value"),
    names_pattern = "(.+)_(AANTAL|GEM)"
  ) |>
  # DUO writes "<5" for small counts -> NA
  mutate(AANTAL = as.numeric(AANTAL)) |>
  filter(!is.na(AANTAL), AANTAL > 0, !is.na(GEM), GEM > 0) |>
  group_by(INSTELLINGSCODE, provider) |>
  summarise(AANTAL = sum(AANTAL), .groups = "drop")

# most schools only use one provider - take whichever tested the most students
primary_provider <- school_provider |>
  group_by(INSTELLINGSCODE) |>
  slice_max(AANTAL, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(INSTELLINGSCODE, provider)

school_weights <- schoolweging |>
  mutate(INSTELLINGSCODE = str_remove(OVT, "\\|.*$")) |>
  group_by(INSTELLINGSCODE) |>
  summarise(
    schoolweging = weighted.mean(schoolweging, w = aantal_leerlingen),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

count_cols <- c(
  "REKENEN_LAGER1F", "REKENEN_1F", "REKENEN_1S",
  "LV_LAGER1F", "LV_1F", "LV_2F",
  "TV_LAGER1F", "TV_1F", "TV_2F"
)

ref_levels <- referentieniveaus |>
  mutate(across(all_of(count_cols), ~ suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.)))) |>
  group_by(INSTELLINGSCODE) |>
  summarise(
    across(all_of(count_cols), ~ sum(.x, na.rm = TRUE)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    rekenen_n = REKENEN_LAGER1F + REKENEN_1F + REKENEN_1S,
    taal_lv_n = LV_LAGER1F + LV_1F + LV_2F,
    taal_tv_n = TV_LAGER1F + TV_1F + TV_2F,
    score = (
      100 * REKENEN_1S / rekenen_n +
        100 * LV_2F / taal_lv_n +
        100 * TV_2F / taal_tv_n
    ) / 3,
    n_students = rekenen_n
  ) |>
  filter(rekenen_n > 0, taal_lv_n > 0, taal_tv_n > 0) |>
  select(INSTELLINGSCODE, score, n_students)

school_data <- ref_levels |>
  inner_join(primary_provider, by = "INSTELLINGSCODE") |>
  left_join(school_weights, by = "INSTELLINGSCODE")
```


### Create plot 

```{r plot-1, fig.height = 6, fig.width = 11.5, fig.align = "center"}
# Element 1:
# ----------

element_1 <- school_data |>
  filter(provider %in% c("LIB", "IEP", "ROUTE8")) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = score, fill = provider, alpha = provider)) +
  geom_density(color = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "IEP"    = "#EB6834",
    "LIB"    = "#2A78D6",
    "ROUTE8" = "#1BAF7A"
  )) +
  scale_alpha_manual(values = c(
    "IEP" = 0.4,
    "LIB" = 0.4,
    "ROUTE8" = 0.4
  )) +
  ylab("Density") +
  xlab("% of students reaching target level, per school") +
  labs(fill = "Test provider") +
  guides(
    color = "none",
    alpha = "none",
    fill = guide_legend(override.aes = list(color = NA))
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(linewidth = 0.7),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )

# Element 2:
# ----------

# Data preparation for element 2:

providers <- school_data |>
  filter(
    provider %in% c("LIB", "IEP", "ROUTE8"),
    !is.na(schoolweging),
    schoolweging >= 22
  ) |>
  mutate(schoolweging_int = floor(schoolweging / 2) * 2) |>
  group_by(provider, schoolweging_int) |>
  summarize(
    score = weighted.mean(score, w = n_students, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

endpoints <- providers |>
  group_by(provider) |>
  slice(c(1, n())) |>
  ungroup()

national_average <- school_data |>
  filter(
    !is.na(schoolweging),
    schoolweging >= 22
  ) |>
  mutate(schoolweging_int = floor(schoolweging / 2) * 2) |>
  group_by(schoolweging_int) |>
  summarize(
    score = weighted.mean(score, w = n_students, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Plotting element 2:

element_2 <- providers |>
  ggplot(aes(x = schoolweging_int, y = score, color = provider)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(data = endpoints, size = 3, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_line(
    data = national_average,
    aes(x = schoolweging_int, y = score),
    color = "#595959",
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = national_average |> slice_max(schoolweging_int, n = 1),
    aes(x = schoolweging_int, y = score, label = "National average"),
    hjust = -0.06,
    size = 3,
    fontface = "italic",
    color = "#595959"
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    name = "Test provider",
    values = c(
      "IEP"    = "#EB6834",
      "LIB"    = "#2A78D6",
      "ROUTE8" = "#1BAF7A"
    ),
    labels = c(
      "IEP"    = "IEP\n(n = 56,483)",
      "LIB"    = "LIB\n(n = 71,120)",
      "ROUTE8" = "ROUTE8\n(n = 7,672)"
    )
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    limits = c(21, 41.5),
    breaks = c(22, 26, 30, 34, 38)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 100)) +
  xlab("School weighting (higher = more disadvantaged)") +
  ylab("% reaching target level") +
  annotate(
    "point",
    x = 29.4, y = 90,
    shape = 21, size = 5,
    fill = "black", color = "black"
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = 29.4, y = 90,
    label = "i", size = 3.8,
    fontface = "bold", family = "serif",
    color = "white"
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = 29.9,
    y = 90,
    label = paste0(
      "Only LIB stays above the national",
      "\naverage at every school weighting"
    ),
    size = 3,
    hjust = 0,
    fontface = "bold.italic",
    color = "#2A78D6"
  ) +
  annotate(
    "curve",
    x = 31, y = 84, xend = 28, yend = 66,
    curvature = 0.3,
    arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.2, "cm")),
    color = "black", linewidth = 0.6
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(linewidth = 0.7),
    legend.position = "top"
  )

# Element 3:
# ----------

element_3 <- ggplot() +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = 0.5, y = 0.5,
    label = paste0(
      "LIB has the highest percentage of students reaching ",
      "the target level, and Route8 the lowest. This gap\n",
      "holds even when accounting for the socio-economic status of schools."
    ),
    fontface = "bold",
    size = 6,
    hjust = 0.5,
    vjust = 0.5,
    family = "serif"
  ) +
  xlim(0, 1) +
  ylim(0, 1) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(plot.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0))

# Combined Plot:
# ----------

cowplot::plot_grid(
  element_3,
  plot_grid(element_1 + theme(legend.position = "none"), element_2, nrow = 1),
  ncol = 1, rel_heights = c(1, 5)
)
```


## **Part B: Interactive visualizations with plotly**


### Prepare data

```{r data-prep-2, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# one row per (school, provider actually used)
school_provider <- eindscores |>
  select(INSTELLINGSCODE, matches("_(AANTAL|GEM)$")) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = matches("_(AANTAL|GEM)$"),
    names_to = c("provider", ".value"),
    names_pattern = "(.+)_(AANTAL|GEM)"
  ) |>
  # DUO writes "<5" for small counts -> NA
  mutate(AANTAL = as.numeric(AANTAL)) |>
  filter(!is.na(AANTAL), AANTAL > 0, !is.na(GEM), GEM > 0) |>
  group_by(INSTELLINGSCODE, provider) |>
  summarise(AANTAL = sum(AANTAL), .groups = "drop")

# one row per school: whichever single provider tested the most of its students
primary_provider <- school_provider |>
  group_by(INSTELLINGSCODE) |>
  slice_max(AANTAL, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(INSTELLINGSCODE, provider)

school_location <- eindscores |>
  select(INSTELLINGSCODE, INSTELLINGSNAAM_VESTIGING, PROVINCIE, GEMEENTENAAM) |>
  group_by(INSTELLINGSCODE) |>
  slice(1) |>
  ungroup()

school_weights <- schoolweging |>
  mutate(INSTELLINGSCODE = str_remove(OVT, "\\|.*$")) |>
  group_by(INSTELLINGSCODE) |>
  summarise(
    schoolweging = weighted.mean(schoolweging, w = aantal_leerlingen),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

count_cols <- c(
  "REKENEN_LAGER1F", "REKENEN_1F", "REKENEN_1S",
  "LV_LAGER1F", "LV_1F", "LV_2F",
  "TV_LAGER1F", "TV_1F", "TV_2F"
)

ref_levels <- referentieniveaus |>
  mutate(across(all_of(count_cols), ~ suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.)))) |>
  group_by(INSTELLINGSCODE) |>
  summarise(
    across(all_of(count_cols), ~ sum(.x, na.rm = TRUE)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    rekenen_n = REKENEN_LAGER1F + REKENEN_1F + REKENEN_1S,
    taal_lv_n = LV_LAGER1F + LV_1F + LV_2F,
    taal_tv_n = TV_LAGER1F + TV_1F + TV_2F,
    score = (
      100 * REKENEN_1S / rekenen_n +
        100 * LV_2F / taal_lv_n +
        100 * TV_2F / taal_tv_n
    ) / 3,
    n_students = rekenen_n
  ) |>
  filter(rekenen_n > 0, taal_lv_n > 0, taal_tv_n > 0) |>
  select(INSTELLINGSCODE, score, n_students)

# a school needs a known provider, a computable score, AND a schoolweging
# value to appear on this chart - unlike Part A's school_data, which kept
# schoolweging-less schools around for its density plot, this scatter has
# no use for a school it can't place on the x-axis
school_data <- ref_levels |>
  inner_join(primary_provider, by = "INSTELLINGSCODE") |>
  inner_join(school_location, by = "INSTELLINGSCODE") |>
  inner_join(school_weights, by = "INSTELLINGSCODE") |>
  filter(!is.na(schoolweging))
```


### Create scatterplot

```{r plot-2_scatter, fig.align="center", fig.height=5, fig.width=7.5, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Preparations for Plotting:
# ----------
scatter_data <- school_data |>
  filter(n_students >= 40) |>
  mutate(
    provider = factor(
      provider,
      levels = c("AMN", "DIA", "DOE", "IEP", "LIB", "ROUTE8")
    ),
    tooltip = paste0(
      "<b>School:</b> ", INSTELLINGSNAAM_VESTIGING,
      "<br><b>Provider:</b> ", provider,
      "<br><b>Doorstroomtoets score:</b> ", round(score, 1), "%",
      "<br><b>School weighting:</b> ", round(schoolweging, 1),
      "<br><b>Students tested:</b> ", n_students,
      "<br><b>Province:</b> ", PROVINCIE,
      "<br><b>Municipality:</b> ", GEMEENTENAAM
    )
  )

provider_colours <- c(
  "AMN"    = "#EEA1BC",
  "DIA"    = "#7A72C3",
  "DOE"    = "#F4B53C",
  "IEP"    = "#F48661",
  "LIB"    = "#4C91DE",
  "ROUTE8" = "#50BE98"
)

# Non-interactive Plot:
# ----------

scatter_plot <- ggplot(
  scatter_data,
  aes(
    x = schoolweging,
    y = score,
    colour = provider,
    size = n_students,
    text = tooltip
  )
) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, stroke = 0.35) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = provider_colours,
    name = "Test provider"
  ) +
  scale_size_continuous(
    name = "Number of Students",
    range = c(1, 6),
    breaks = c(40, 60, 80, 100, 120)
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(20, 25, 30, 35),
    minor_breaks = seq(20, 37.5, by = 2.5)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = c(25, 50, 75, 100),
    minor_breaks = seq(12.5, 100, by = 12.5)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Doorstroomtoets score by school weighting, per school",
    subtitle = "Showing schools with 40 or more students",
    x = "School weighting (higher = more disadvantaged)",
    y = "% reaching target level"
  ) +
  guides(
    colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 2)),
    size = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = c(2, 3, 4, 5, 6),
                                            colour = "grey30"))
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    panel.border = element_rect(colour = "grey25", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.5),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(colour = "grey88", linewidth = 0.4),
    panel.grid.minor = element_line(colour = "grey93"),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 15, colour = "black"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, colour = "black"),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 12),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 10)
  )

scatter_plot
```


### Create interactive plot

```{r plot-2_interactive, fig.align="center", fig.height=5, fig.width=7.5, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
interactive_scatter <- ggplotly(
  scatter_plot,
  tooltip = "text"
) |>
  layout(
    title = list(
      text = paste0(
        "Doorstroomtoets score by school weighting, per school",
        "<br><sup>Showing schools with 40 or more students</sup>"
      ),
      x = 0
    ),
    legend = list(
      title = list(text = "Test provider")
    ),
    hoverlabel = list(
      bgcolor = "white",
      bordercolor = "grey50",
      font = list(color = "black", size = 13)
    )
  )


interactive_scatter
```
